<USER_SCRIPT>
CORAL — A SUMMER LAUNCH

Bondi Studio - Morning in front of her microphone

Sunlight floods a white vanity. SCARLETT (19, blonde, sun-kissed),
a Bondi influencer, unboxes a coral lipstick and turns it slowly
to camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
One shade. One summer.

CLOSE ON THE TUBE — the coral bullet twists up and catches the
light. Scarlett smiles at her reflection, the colour already hers.

EXT. BONDI BEACH PROMENADE - CONTINUOUS

Scarlett walks the promenade, blonde hair lifting in the breeze,
surfers cresting behind her. She glances back at camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
Made for the water. Wear it everywhere.

EXT. BONDI BEACH - SHORELINE - CONTINUOUS

She laughs as a wave breaks at her feet. The lipstick lands
beside the brand mark in the sand.

SUPER:  CORAL.  OUT NOW.
</USER_SCRIPT>

Target video duration: 1 minute (about 8-12 scenes). Give each scene a realistic single-clip duration — most around 5 seconds, a few up to ~8 when the motion genuinely needs it — and label it in the script (e.g. a "Scene 3 — 5s" heading). Reach the target length through the number of scenes, not by stretching clips or padding with repeated beats.

Style & genre (let this drive WHAT HAPPENS, not just the look):
- Style: Product Ad / ecommerce
- About: Fresh, tactile product content with lifestyle context and sensory detail. Designed for Instagram, DTC brands, e-commerce, and social-first campaigns.
- Genre cues: ecommerce, product, instagram, dtc, lifestyle, social

Style context (apply these aesthetics throughout):
- Mood: Fresh, sensory, and effortlessly cool
- Art style: Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save
- Lighting: Bright natural window light with clean directional shadows. Direct on-camera flash for punchy editorial energy on select shots. No heavy diffusion -- let light feel real and immediate. Warm late-afternoon glow for lifestyle moments. High-key and airy overall with pops of contrast
- Color palette: #FFFFFF, #F0E6D3, #D4536D, #1A1A1A, #E8F4E8
- Color grading: Clean and bright with true-to-life color. Whites are crisp, skin tones warm and natural. Minimal processing -- the product looks like it does in your hand. Slight warmth in highlights, lifted shadows keeping everything airy. One accent color pops against neutral base
- Camera work: Dynamic mix of handheld and locked shots with consistent energy. Handheld with natural micro-movement for lifestyle moments -- hands interacting, daily rituals, real context. Quick-cut to locked beauty frames for hero product shots. Macro details on textures and surfaces. Overhead flat-lays directly above. Eye-level and slightly above angles. Shallow depth of field on tactile details. Energetic pacing -- no lingering, every frame earns its time
- Reference works: modern social-first skincare-brand content, dewy minimalist beauty-brand visual identity, sun-soaked lifestyle beauty campaigns, playful color-blocked skincare content

Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape — favor wide, cinematic compositions

response.content:
Scene 1 — 5s
EXT. BONDI BEACH CAR PARK - EARLY MORNING
A sun-faded canvas tote slams onto the warm white bonnet of a parked sedan, ocean a bright strip beyond the rail. SCARLETT (19, salt-stiff blonde hair, black rashie half-peeled, sandy calves) upends the bag. Sunscreen and a cracked hair claw spill out; a slim coral lipstick tube tumbles after them and she snatches it from the air.

Scene 2 — 6s
She leans into the driver's side mirror, hard morning light cutting a clean shadow across the door. She twists the coral bullet up and paints her mouth in one unfussy pass, then presses her lips together. No vanity, no posing — just a local getting it on before the water.

Scene 3 — 5s
She thumbs the cap back on, drops the tube into the tote, and slings the bag over one shoulder in the same motion. Flip-flops slap the car-park concrete as she walks toward the promenade, chrome and white paint flashing behind her.

Scene 4 — 5s
EXT. BONDI PROMENADE - MORNING
Wide along the promenade: joggers, a rack of rental boards, pale concrete. MAISIE (20, freckled, spring suit peeled to her waist, a foam board under one arm) falls in beside Scarlett and clocks the fresh coral mouth, already grinning.

MAISIE
You're going in with that on?

Scene 5 — 5s
Scarlett doesn't break stride. She glances over, the coral breaking into a real grin, sun on her cheekbones.

SCARLETT
That's the point.

She breaks into a jog toward the sand, tote bouncing, hair lifting.

Scene 6 — 6s
EXT. BONDI SHORELINE
She dumps the tote above the waterline and runs straight into a breaking wave, arms up. Whitewater hits her midriff and a laugh punches out of her, coral mouth bright against the spray, 16:9 shoreline stretching either side.

Scene 7 — 5s
She comes up slicked and blinking, wipes salt from her eyes with the back of her wrist — not her mouth. A smaller wave slaps her shoulder and she turns, wading for shore, the colour still sharp as wet hair ropes down her back.

Scene 8 — 5s
On the sand she yanks a crumpled white shirt over her head; a hard on-camera flash pops as her face comes through, coral hitting first, shirt still settling on wet rashie. She shakes her hair out of the collar and the fabric drops into place.

Scene 9 — 5s
The lipstick has rolled from the open tote into the coarse sand. Her wet fingers pick it up, turn it once — grit on the casing, coral lacquer catching the sun — and she does not twist it open. She tucks it into the tote's inner pocket and stands.

Scene 10 — 5s
EXT. BONDI PROMENADE - LATE AFTERNOON
Warm late light, high-key and a little gold. Scarlett walks the rail with a dripping mango ice and takes a real bite from the side. Juice beads at the corner of her mouth; she thumbs it away. The coral stays, lived-in, not ruined.

Scene 11 — 6s
She stops at the rail above the beach and leans on it, watching the next set roll through. Then she turns her face into the wind and the last of the sun, eyes closing, a private almost-smile. Hair lifts. The coral catches the light. She does not check a phone. She does not reapply. She just stays.
